title: General task team
description: Select relevant available specialists for any scoped task: research, review, implementation, or explicitly authorized actions.
intent: Complete the user's actual task using the smallest useful specialist team. These are conditional candidates, not an all-agent run. Infer action boundaries from the request and existing authorization; selecting this preset alone does not authorize source changes or external actions.

assignments.task: Gather cited current sources and compare options against the project decision criteria. Return an evidence packet for later validation.
assignments.when: The task needs external research, current or niche facts, a technology/product/market comparison, or source discovery.

assignments.task: Map accepted requirements, actual implementation states, relevant gates, and evidence gaps without updating trackers.
assignments.when: The task asks about scope, progress, readiness, or a broad project review.

assignments.task: Review structural options, contracts, ownership, failure paths, and consequential trade-offs.
assignments.when: The task asks for architecture or changes public contracts, persistence, or system boundaries.

assignments.task: Assess visual/system fit, components, UI states, contrast, spacing, and responsive consistency; complete journey design belongs to ux-designer.
assignments.when: The task asks for design or changes a user-facing interface.

assignments.task: Review existing correctness and test evidence without editing; identify meaningful checks for the requested task.
assignments.when: The task requests a correctness/test audit or needs a defect reproduced before implementation.

assignments.task: Review relevant trust boundaries, reachable weaknesses, and secure requirements using scoped evidence.
assignments.when: The task requests security review or concerns sensitive data, authorization, tenancy, or untrusted inputs.

assignments.task: Inspect existing measurements, reproduce scoped bottlenecks where authorized, and establish comparable budgets.
assignments.when: The task asks about performance, resource cost, or an optimization that needs baseline evidence.

assignments.task: Independently check existing claims, calculations, datasets, and provenance. Do not validate unfinished results from parallel research.
assignments.when: The task primarily questions existing evidence, factual claims, or calculations.

assignments.task: Establish release gates, artifact scope, compatibility, rollback, and action boundaries without publishing.
assignments.when: The task concerns a release, artifacts, deployment readiness, or recovery.

assignments.task: Design/review the empirical method, hypotheses, controls, uncertainty, and requested execution boundary; do not run unrequested experiments.
assignments.when: The task asks for experiments, empirical evaluation, or causal interpretation.

assignments.task: Develop or check the mathematical formulation, derivation, assumptions, numerical stability, and error bounds.
assignments.when: The task requires mathematical reasoning, quantitative algorithms, or consequential formulas.

assignments.task: Analyze approved data with explicit grain, metrics, denominators, provenance, and uncertainty; return results without mutating datasets.
assignments.when: The task asks about datasets, behavior metrics, funnels, cohorts, or quantitative interpretation.

assignments.task: Define bounded requirements, priorities, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes from accepted goals.
assignments.when: The task asks for product definition, prioritization, or acceptance criteria.

assignments.task: Analyze supplied user evidence or design a bounded study; preserve the distinction between assumptions and observations.
assignments.when: The task needs user-needs or usability research.

assignments.task: Return requested copy/drafts using approved facts, voice, channel, and supported claims.
assignments.when: The task asks for writing, editing, product copy, or campaign wording.

assignments.task: Develop evidence-backed positioning, audience/message strategy, or campaign hypotheses.
assignments.when: The task asks for marketing direction, positioning, segmentation, or campaign strategy.

assignments.task: Plan distribution, launch sequencing, pricing hypotheses, acquisition/sales motion, readiness, and measurement.
assignments.when: The task asks for go-to-market or commercial launch planning.

assignments.task: Review search eligibility, technical/content SEO, and available measured discovery evidence.
assignments.when: The task concerns conventional search discoverability or SEO.

assignments.task: Review actual/provided AI-answer visibility, citations, factual representation, sampling, and access gaps.
assignments.when: The task concerns generative-engine optimization or AI-answer visibility.

assignments.task: Assess or draft the specified locale adaptation, terminology, formats, and UI behavior.
assignments.when: The task requests translation/localization or international UI behavior.

assignments.task: Define or review mechanics, progression, balance, economies, and player-experience hypotheses.
assignments.when: The task concerns game systems or gameplay design.

assignments.task: Establish or review the requested asset brief, actual artifacts, tool availability, visual intent, export, and provenance.
assignments.when: The task concerns 3D modeling, materials, lighting, animation, or asset creation.

assignments.task: Review art/runtime integration, shaders, asset pipelines, rendering constraints, and actual budgets.
assignments.when: The task concerns visual-runtime integration or rendering/asset tooling.

assignments.task: Map or design requested complete task journeys, transitions, information hierarchy, continuity, and recovery from actual project context.
assignments.when: The task concerns user experience, navigation, coherent flows, decision burden, or journey design.

assignments.task: Independently walk through existing tasks and identify evidence-linked confusion, repeated work, dead ends, context loss, or recovery failures.
assignments.when: The task asks for usability review or reproduced task friction.

assignments.task: Assess scoped semantics, keyboard/focus, assistive use, contrast, targets, motion, and reflow with actual evidence and declared criteria.
assignments.when: The task requests deep accessibility review or involves consequential access barriers.

assignments.task: Establish relevant accepted Definition of Done, integrated behavior, target, baseline, and gate evidence requirements without source/tracker changes.
assignments.when: The task requests increment releasability, iteration closure, or implementation of a product increment.

assignments.task: Implement requested code/configuration/test/documentation changes with checks and preserved user work. For specialist assets, content, localization, or analysis artifacts, the coordinator may replace this candidate with the capable domain owner under the same exclusive-writer rules.
assignments.when: The user requests implementation, fixes, refactoring, or saved/created artifacts; research or review alone does not satisfy this condition. Use the appropriate available domain specialist as the exclusive owner for specialist artifacts.

assignments.task: Prepare the explicitly requested version/changelog/artifacts and run release checks after any implementation writer has finished. Do not tag, publish, or deploy in this stage.
assignments.when: The user explicitly requests release preparation or execution requiring release artifact changes.

assignments.task: Independently review the completed changed snapshot and actual correctness/regression checks without editing.
assignments.when: Meaningful code or release-artifact changes need verification, or the user requests an independent quality check.

assignments.task: Review the completed UI snapshot against accepted flows, system components, states, and accessibility evidence.
assignments.when: Implementation changed a user-facing interface and a design check is relevant.

assignments.task: Review completed changes at affected trust/data boundaries.
assignments.when: Implementation changed security-sensitive boundaries or controls.

assignments.task: Verify performance claims or budgets against comparable baseline evidence.
assignments.when: Implementation changes a measured hot path or claims an optimization/budget outcome.

assignments.task: Check material research conclusions, citations, calculations, or public claims after the evidence packet or changed artifact is complete.
assignments.when: New material factual, comparative, quantitative, or provenance claims affect the requested decision or deliverable.

assignments.task: Inspect or run applicable isolated artifact/consumer/startup checks or reuse current retained evidence, then reconcile required technical gates. Avoid shared output collisions and preserve source; do not publish in this review stage.
assignments.when: A release was prepared, readiness/execution is requested, or the product increment has applicable accepted artifact/consumer/startup gates.

assignments.task: Check completed 3D/runtime/shader assets or integration against actual compatible tool outputs.
assignments.when: Implementation created or changed visual runtime assets/integration and an independent domain check is relevant.

assignments.task: Independently walk through completed changed task paths, checking feedback, continuity, alternatives, and recovery without editing.
assignments.when: Implementation materially changes user task journeys or an independent usability check is requested.

assignments.task: Check affected completed UI states with declared criteria and actual keyboard/assistive evidence where available.
assignments.when: Implementation affects semantics, focus, forms, accessible interaction, targets, reflow, or another meaningful access boundary.

assignments.task: Reconcile completed specialist and artifact results for the integrated product after verification. Report ready, blocked, or unverified for the named target/snapshot and recheck affected gates after corrections before dependent delivery actions.
assignments.when: The task requests integrated product readiness/iteration closure or implements a product increment; unrelated research or draft artifacts do not require this stage.

assignments.task: Perform only explicitly requested commit or push operations for verified changes, respecting repository instructions and checking resulting state.
assignments.when: The user explicitly authorizes the specified commit/push and its prerequisite checks are complete.

assignments.task: Execute only explicitly authorized tagging, publication, or deployment after required readiness gates pass; verify actual external state and recovery information.
assignments.when: The user explicitly authorizes the specific release operation, target, and scope, and required technical/integrated readiness gates pass for its actual snapshot; blocked or unverified required gates prevent this dependent delivery.

assignments.task: Update only explicitly authorized tracker entries backed by completed acceptance evidence; verify saved state.
assignments.when: The user explicitly authorizes the specific tracker update and its completion evidence is available.

completion: The requested research answer, review, implementation, or authorized action is complete with actual evidence; irrelevant stages are skipped.
Selected specialists are available and scoped; additional project specialists honor the same limits and action boundaries.
New research is validated after gathering, changed source is checked after writing, and dependent actions wait for verified prerequisites.
Applicable findings and contradictions are reconciled; unfinished, failed, or unavailable checks remain explicit.
Report a concise result, selected roles, material changes/checks, and unresolved gaps without claiming every candidate ran.
Product-increment readiness is reconciled after completed checks and before dependent delivery; existing evidence is reused only while current, and no automatic CI trigger is claimed.
